summary.headline: VTM Ltd FY26 PAT fell about 75% to Rs 11 crore on US tariff discounts (~Rs 20 crore), with FY27 turnover guided up 12-14% and EBITDA margin targeted at 10-11%.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 8% (base ~Rs 372 crore) but PAT of about Rs 11 crore, down roughly 75% YoY. The drop was attributed to an ~18% US tariff-related discount (~Rs 20 crore), chargeback discounts (~Rs 8 crore), a Rs 2.3 crore forex MTM loss on PCFC borrowings, a gratuity provision under the new Labour Code, and ~15% higher raw material costs. FY26 EBITDA margin was 7.43%, and management said the 18% discount to the US customer Quince is still in place, with negotiations ongoing and the current price point at about 10%. Management guided to 12-14% FY27 top-line growth, a 10-11% EBITDA margin, and a 6.5 million-unit order backlog as of 31 May.

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs 372 crore (Rs 420 crore implied at 12-14% growth for FY27)

financial_highlights.metric: PBT normalised for tariff, chargebacks, MTM

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs 1 crore; total comprehensive income Rs 2.32 crore
~Rs 150 crore (vs Rs 92 crore previously); inventory turnover 122 days

segments.name: Home textiles (cut-and-sew, made-ups)
segments.commentary: Roughly 52% of FY26 revenue (~Rs 190-192 crore); about 50% of that is commodity items, with the rest value-added and top-of-bed. Exports are FOB, and the tariff discount is concentrated here. Export sales to non-US countries were about Rs 16-17 crore (~10% of export volume).

segments.name: Greige fabrics
segments.commentary: The remaining ~48% of revenue (~Rs 180 crore) in FY26. Exports are CIF. Management says greige fabric earns a traditional 7-9% margin, and utilisation runs at 80-83%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at 12-14%, and a 10-15% turnover increase cited in the prepared remarks.
FY27 EBITDA margin target of 10-11%; management called a return to ~19% a likely 'audacious goal' in the post-tariff era.

Management targets a run-rate revenue of Rs 500-600 crore with the right product mix, full outsourcing capacity utilisation and higher realisations. Timing is 'maybe this year, or next financial year'.
No further capex planned in FY27; the capex cycle is over, with new looms commissioning in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Inventory expected to return to prior-year levels within two quarters, via lean practices and an industrial engineering consultant.
New customers in the UK, Europe, Middle East, Japan and Australia; onboarding takes about one year, with results expected in 2-3 quarters.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about Rs 25 crore; investments from FY25 are only now coming into full operation in FY27.
Greige fabric utilisation runs at 80-83%; company-wide operating efficiency about 80%, which management says will remain at that level.
Additional looms installed in FY26 to come into production in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Home textiles outsourcing is increasing; commodity items may be outsourced to cut costs and expand volume.
demand_pricing: Order backlog of about 6.5 million units as of 31 May (the CFO also cited ~6 million); volume growth in FY26 about 15%, with 15-20% guided for FY27 on the current order book. Management said volume growth will not fully translate into sales because of price realisation drops.

US tariff rose to ~50-60% at one point and then settled at 18%; the company shared ~10% of the tariff burden with the customer through a discount of 18% that is still in place, against a current tariff of 10%.
Customer Quince (US) is a major account; management said the discount is under negotiation and a slight price increase has been agreed on one or two products from this quarter.
Customer price sensitivity is elevated post-tariff; management cited the tariff, the war and oil price shocks as exogenous hits.
Input costs: raw material up ~15% due to the war and cotton futures moving to 78 cents from ~69-70 cents; bleaching, job work and freight costs also rose.
Working capital: payables held to 45-60 days; the company says it pays vendors within 45 days to comply with MSME rules.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 operating margin return to FY25 levels of ~19% EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: uncertain. FY26 was 7.43%; target is 10-11%. CMD said 19% is pre-tariff and may be a stretch in the post-tariff era.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said greige runs at 80-83% utilisation so ~80% is the practical ceiling. Management said the top line would reach ~Rs 420 crore at peak, with a Rs 500-600 crore run-rate possible with the right mix and outsourcing.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin split between greige and home textiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Greige fabric earns a traditional 7-9% margin. The EBITDA drop is mainly from home textiles, where the ~Rs 20 crore tariff-linked price cut was the main hit, plus gratuity (Rs 41 lakh) and PF settlement (Rs 32 lakh) costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 18% discount still in place when US tariffs have fallen to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount is still in place, the customer is more price sensitive post-tariff, and negotiations are ongoing; pipeline sales carry the earlier tariff.

qa_highlights.question: Why are payables so low compared with group companies?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said both companies are cash-rich and pay vendors within 30-45 days, so terms are not favourable to group entities. Pacific Cotton is a separate US entity selling basic lower-value Amazon-brand items.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 discounting fall from Rs 13.7 crore to Rs 2.3 crore, yet gross margin is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: gross margin is unchanged; Q4 PBT Rs 4.1 crore vs Rs 4.87 crore in Q3, with the gap from strategy consultant costs, the PF settlement and a Rs 62 lakh Canadian liability.

risks_watch: Tariff discount of 18% still applied to Quince despite the US tariff falling to 10%; the outcome of negotiations is the key swing factor for margins.
Inventory rose to ~Rs 150 crore from Rs 92 crore; inventory turnover is ~2.5x revenue and management targets a return to prior-year levels within two quarters.
PCFC forex borrowings (~Rs 64 crore restated) carry MTM exposure to the rupee; the Rs 2.3 crore hit recurred in FY26.
Raw material inflation (~15%) with cotton at 78 cents; freight, bleaching and job work costs are rising.
Quince customer concentration; management declined to give a 2030 geographic mix or long-term revenue projection.
New market (UK, Europe, Japan, Australia) onboarding takes about a year; results expected in 2-3 quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on recovery and new markets but defensive on margins and the Quince discount; several answers were brief or deferred ('too early to give a projection', 'negotiations are going on'). Management attributed the profit fall to exogenous factors (tariffs, war, oil) and gave few hard numbers on the customer discount.
key_quotes: We are being a little conservative on that front. But we're definitely not understating here.

adds.what: Additional looms installed in FY26 coming into production

growth.why: Management guides 12-14% FY27 top-line growth, backed by a 6.5 million-unit order backlog (15-20% volume growth guided on current orders) and new looms coming online in Q1-Q2 FY27, though no firm capacity numbers were given and price realisation drops offset volume gains.
